message.content:
Below is a ready‑to‑run **gcloud** CLI command that creates a new Compute Engine VM on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
(If you prefer the raw REST API payload, see the section below.)

```bash
# 1️⃣  Set your project ID and zone
PROJECT_ID="YOUR_PROJECT_ID"
ZONE="us-central1-a"

# 2️⃣  Create a new VM named “rtx-a6000-demo”
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-demo"

# 3️⃣  Pick a machine type that can host the GPU (e.g., n1-standard-8)
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"

# 4️⃣  Specify the GPU type and count
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a6000"
GPU_COUNT=1

# 5️⃣  Use the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# 6️⃣  Optional: set a startup script to install CUDA drivers
STARTUP_SCRIPT=$(cat <<EOF
#!/bin/bash
apt-get update
apt-get install -y cuda-drivers
EOF
)

# 7️⃣  Build the command
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
    --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
    --zone="$ZONE" \
    --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
    --accelerator=count=$GPU_COUNT,type=$GPU_TYPE \
    --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \
    --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \
    --boot-disk-size=100GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
    --tags=http-server,https-server \
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform

# 8️⃣  Save the startup script to a file (optional)
echo "$STARTUP_SCRIPT" > startup.sh
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--project` | Target GCP project |
| `--zone` | Compute zone (e.g., `us-central1-a`) |
| `--machine-type` | CPU & RAM allocation (`n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPU + 30 GB RAM) |
| `--accelerator` | Attach GPUs (`count=1,type=nvidia-tesla-a6000`) |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Base OS image (Ubuntu 20.04 LTS) |
| `--boot-disk-size` / `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk size |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Run a shell script at first boot (installs CUDA drivers) |
| `--tags` | Allow HTTP/HTTPS traffic via firewall rules |
| `--scopes` | Grant full Cloud Platform access (needed for GPU driver installation) |

> **Tip:** If you need more memory or CPUs, change `MACHINE_TYPE` to something like `n1-highmem-16`. Just make sure the selected machine type supports the GPU you’re attaching.

---

## REST API Payload (JSON)

If you’d rather use the Compute Engine REST API directly, here’s a minimal JSON body you can POST to:

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-demo",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [{ "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y cuda-drivers"
      }
    ]
  },
  "tags": { "items": ["http-server", "https-server"] }
}
```

Send this payload to:

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/instances
```

Make sure you replace `YOUR_PROJECT_ID` with your actual GCP project ID and adjust the zone if needed.

---

### Quick Checklist Before Running

1. **Billing enabled** – Ensure billing is active for the target project.  
2. **API enabled** – Enable the *Compute Engine API* in the Cloud Console.  
3. **Permissions** – You need `roles/compute.admin` or equivalent.  
4. **Quota** – Verify you have enough GPU quota in the chosen zone.  

Once the instance boots, the startup script installs the CUDA drivers automatically, so you’ll be ready to run GPU workloads right away. Happy hacking!
